papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of pairwise classical, quantum and mixed kernel combinations in multiple kernel learning with SVMs, plus a trainable weighting network called QCC-net.

assertions.value: The authors report that, among three quantum and three classical kernels, only the most complex and parametric quantum kernel (QAOA) attains a higher optimum weight in pairwise combination with the most performant classical kernel (RBF), and that the classical RBF kernel and its combinations performed best overall.
quotes: only the most complex and parametric quantum kernel (QAOA) attains higher a optimum weight in pairwise combination with the most performant classical kernel (RBF)
More broadly, classical RBF kernel and its combinations performed the best overall.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study on synthetic data.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum-kernel combination beat the classical RBF kernel in this study, so the paper gives no empirical quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that each dataset instance was a synthetic binary classification set of 100 samples, with d = 2 to 13 features, and that kernel metrics are medians over 120 instances.
quotes: Each dataset instance consisted of 100 samples
Median kernel metrics over 120 instances, across datasets with d = 2 to 13 features
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup (Section IV.B, Fig. 4 caption).

assertions.value: The authors state that the work investigates simulated quantum kernels, and that experiments on datasets with a different, less generic structure may give more promising results for quantum-quantum and quantum-classical combinations.
quotes: this work investigates simulated quantum kernels in the context of multiple kernel learning
experiments on datasets with a different, less generic structure may provide the more promising results for q.q. and q.c. combinations
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract and Section V state the simulated, generic-data scope of the study.
assertions.reader_inference: The results do not speak to quantum hardware or to structured real-world data.

papers.title_in_file: Learning Circuits with Infinite Tensor Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, T-count reduction section, discussion; the methods and the other result sections were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A method that uses infinite matrix product states to compile shallow translation-invariant circuits for ground-state preparation and time evolution, with a T-count comparison against Trotterization.

assertions.value: The authors report that, after decomposition into the Clifford+T gate set, their iMPS-optimized circuits for the unitary e^{-iHt} of the TFIM Hamiltonian with t = 2.0 need up to a 5.2 fold reduction in T-count compared with Trotterized circuits.
quotes: after decomposing into the Clifford+T gate set we similarly find an advantage, with up to a 5.2
for the TFIM Hamiltonian with t = 2.0, into the Clifford+T gate set
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result for one Hamiltonian (TFIM) and one evolution time.
assertions.reader_inference: The reduction is shown on a single 1D model, so it does not establish a general fault-tolerant advantage.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in time-evolution simulations, their iMPS-optimized circuits are more efficient in 2-qubit gate depth than all Trotterizations tested.
quotes: in simulations involving time-evolution are found to be more efficient in 2-qubit gate depth than all Trotterizations tested
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical comparison against the Trotter orders tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus on translation-invariant states and unitaries with a 2-site unit cell, and name extension to infinite 2D systems as future work.
quotes: Throughout this work, we focus on compiling translation invariant states and unitaries with a 2-site unit cell
Future work could explore extending these methods to be scalably applied to infinite 2D systems
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope (Section II text and Section IV Discussion).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Synthetic Data Generation for Industrial Bioprocess Monitoring
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, framework and setup, results, discussion, conclusions; the background sections were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A quantum Wasserstein GAN with a parameterized quantum circuit generator that makes synthetic optical-density time series for a photobioreactor.

assertions.value: The authors report a Dynamic Time Warping score of 0.6843 for their QGAN-generated synthetic data, which they state is lower than the 1.954 reported in a cited financial-data study.
quotes: Our Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) score (0.6843) shown in Figure 10 is lower than that reported in
(1.954), indicating that our QGAN-generated synthetic data more accurately capture the temporal dynamics
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical result on one bioprocess dataset, compared with a number from a different dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: A DTW score on a bioprocess series and one on financial data are not on a common scale, so the comparison does not show the data are better. No classical GAN baseline was seen in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum circuit has five qubits in three layers and that the model was trained for 2000 epochs with a batch size of 20.
quotes: The quantum circuit of our model, shown in 4, comprises five qubits arranged in three layers.
We trained the model for 2000 epochs.
is equal to 20.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup (Section 4).

assertions.value: The authors state that current quantum hardware limitations, including limited qubit counts, decoherence and noise, restrict applicability to larger, more complex datasets.
quotes: Current quantum hardware limitations, including limited qubit counts, decoherence, and noise, restrict applicability to larger, more complex datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit (Section 6, Discussion).

assertions.value: The authors state that their results suggest quantum circuits can efficiently represent complex multivariate probability distributions typical of bioprocess data, potentially offering computational advantages over classical approaches when working with limited datasets.
quotes: Our results suggest that quantum circuits can efficiently represent complex multivariate probability distributions typical of bioprocess data, potentially offering computational advantages over classical approaches when working with limited datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's claim; a classical comparison was not seen in the sections read.
assertions.reader_inference: The reader found no classical baseline run for this paper in the sections read, so the advantage is not shown.

papers.title_in_file: Opportunities and limitations of explaining quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, summary of limitations, numerical results and Section V; the appendix derivations were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A perspective on explainability for quantum machine learning that proposes two explanation methods for parametrized quantum circuit models and tests them on a synthetic task.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose two explanation methods designed for quantum machine learning models, a Taylor decomposition method and quantum layerwise relevance propagation (QLRP), for models based on parametrized quantum circuits.
quotes: We additionally propose two explanation methods designed specifically for quantum machine learning models
quantum layerwise relevance propagation, QLRP
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposed methods with derivations and one synthetic-task experiment; novelty is the authors' claim.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical experiment is a proof of concept on synthetic data, not a claim that quantum models explain better than classical ones nor that their techniques beat established ones; the numerics show that methods perform differently for different tasks and metrics.
quotes: Our goal is to display the practical application of our protocols, not to claim that quantum models have an advantage over classical algorithms in terms of explainability, nor that our proposed explanation techniques are superior to previously-established ones.
different methods perform differently for different tasks and under different metrics
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scope of its numerics (Section IV, Section V).

assertions.value: The authors state that the main challenge they met is scalability, because fully characterizing the Hilbert space of a quantum computation quickly becomes classically intractable.
quotes: Arguably the main challenge we encountered is that of scalability.
the straightforward approach of fully characterizing the Hilbert space of quantum computation quickly becomes classically intractable
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit (Section V).

assertions.value: The authors state it is their understanding that strong evidence for QML models that perform well on practically-relevant tasks is still missing.
quotes: strong evidence for QML models that perform well on practically-relevant tasks is still missing
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' characterization of the field, supported by a citation in the paper, not by a study of their own.

papers.title_in_file: A supplemental investigation of non-linearity in quantum generative models with respect to simulatability and optimization
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2302.00788 v2 (29 Apr 2024). Its title matches the record; the file name carries the earlier v1 title, Generative Modeling with Quantum Neurons.
papers.what_it_is: A follow-up study of the quantum neuron Born machine that asks whether its repeat-until-success non-linearity makes it classically simulatable and whether it makes training unstable.

assertions.value: The authors state that the repeat-until-success sub-routines do not allow the quantum model to be trivially mapped to a classical model, and that this strongly suggests the non-linearity makes the model classically inefficient to simulate.
quotes: we demonstrate that the RUS sub-routines do not allow us to trivially map this quantum model to a classical one
This strongly suggests that the proposed form of non-linearity makes the model classically in-efficient to simulate.
assertions.certainty_reason: An argument that one construction fails, stated as strong suggestion; no hardness proof.
assertions.reader_inference: The result rules out one simulation route, the deferred measurement principle; it does not prove classical hardness.

assertions.value: The authors show that the linearized version of the model, without the repeat-until-success non-linearity, can be sampled classically with O(E) calculations, where E is the number of edges in the network, because it is a Bayesian network.
quotes: one can sample efficiently and classically from the whole network with O(E) calculations, where E is the number of edges in the whole network
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation in Section 3.1 (Bayesian network construction).

assertions.value: The authors report that a (5, 0, 6) quantum neuron network trained on three target distributions reaches strong results in some trials, but with high variance across trials for certain datasets, and that training on the Discrete Gaussian is markedly volatile.
quotes: we train a (5, 0, 6) network on three types of target probability distributions
training on the Discrete Gaussian distribution is markedly volatile
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulation of one network size on three distributions.

assertions.value: The authors state that further evidence is required before larger claims can be made about whether non-linearity of this kind is important for quantum architectures.
quotes: Further evidence is required to make larger claims around whether this feature of classical ML is important for quantum architectures.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit (Section 4, Outlook).

papers.title_in_file: Learning functions of quantum states with distributed architectures
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, resource scaling, discussion and conclusions; the numerical results section was read in outline.
papers.what_it_is: A study of distributed quantum extreme learning machine architectures that learn linear and nonlinear properties of quantum states using computational-basis measurements.

assertions.value: The authors state that spatial multiplexing gives a linear improvement in the required reservoir dimension compared with a single three-layer QELM, with each unit operating independently.
quotes: this corresponds to a linear improvement in the required reservoir dimension
showing a linear reduction in resource requirements per unit
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived from the analytical expressions in Eqs. 5 and 8, Section V.

assertions.value: The authors report that any polynomial target with a nonlinearity of order k can be reconstructed using k reservoirs in their distributed entangled architecture, though specific targets can be recovered with fewer.
quotes: any target exhibiting a nonlinearity of order k can be reconstructed using k reservoirs
assertions.certainty_reason: Reported from the paper's numerical study of polynomial targets.

assertions.value: The authors report that for Renyi entropy and entanglement measures, perfect reconstruction was not achieved with the limited number of reservoirs used, while the error decreased consistently as the number of reservoirs increased.
quotes: perfect reconstruction is not achieved with the limited number of reservoirs used
the error consistently decreases as the number of reservoirs increases
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work consists of numerical simulations and that testing on NISQ quantum hardware platforms is left for future work, including the noise robustness of the models.
quotes: Beyond numerical simulations, the appeal of this approach is in its testing in experiments in NISQ quantum hardware platforms
understanding the noise robustness of these models is crucial
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit (Section VI).

papers.title_in_file: Q2SAR: A Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning Approach for Drug Discovery
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2506.14920 v4 (15 Dec 2025).
papers.what_it_is: A QSAR classification study that compares a simulated quantum-kernel SVM with a classical gradient boosting model on a DYRK1A inhibitor dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that their QMKL-SVM approach reached an AUC of 0.875 against 0.804 for a classical gradient boosting baseline on the DYRK1A inhibitor test set.
quotes: achieved a superior AUC score (0.875 vs. 0.804) on the DYRK1A inhibitor dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, one train-test split.
assertions.reader_inference: The baseline was a default scikit-learn gradient boosting model on 4 PCA features, so the gap does not show a quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the raw data for 1291 molecules were curated to a final dataset of 354 unique molecules, and that PCA reduced the features to four components that capture 37.1% of the total variance.
assertions.anchor: Section III.A, data curation and dimensionality reduction
quotes: The raw data for 1291 molecules underwent rigorous curation
The final dataset comprised 354 unique molecules.
This aggressive reduction to four components, which capture 37.1% of the total variance
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own data and preprocessing setup (Section III).

assertions.value: The authors state that the results reported correspond to the SVM trained on the single, best-aligned kernel identified by kernel-target alignment selection.
quotes: the results reported in this paper correspond to the SVM trained on the single, best-aligned kernel identified through this process.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of what the reported model is (Section III.B).
assertions.reader_inference: The reported model is one kernel, not a weighted combination of several kernels, despite the multiple kernel learning framing.

assertions.value: The authors acknowledge that the study relies on a single train-test split.
quotes: We acknowledge the limitations of this study, including the reliance on a single train-test split
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit (Section VI).

papers.title_in_file: Machine Learning for Quantum Computing Specialists
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and caveats, the NISQ kernel passage, the GAN passage and the conclusion; the classical ML tutorial sections were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A tutorial review that introduces classical machine learning concepts to quantum computing specialists preparing to study quantum machine learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that the review is not a complete review of the current status of QML and is written for readers who already know quantum computing.
assertions.anchor: Section 1.2, Quantum machine learning: some caveats
quotes: Be aware though, that is not a complete review of the current status of QML.
This review is written for those who already some quantum computing knowledge
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope (Section 1.2 and Section 1).

assertions.value: The authors state that this is the age of NISQ devices with high error rates and few qubits, and that increasing physical qubits and getting error correction to work will take at least a decade, and probably much longer.
assertions.anchor: Section 1.2, Quantum machine learning: some caveats
quotes: We are in the age of Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum devices (NISQ) with high error rates and few qubits.
Increasing the number of physical qubits and getting error correction working properly will take at least a decade, and probably much longer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement about the state of the field; the timeline is an opinion.

assertions.value: The authors describe a 2022 paper by Albrecht and others that ran a quantum kernel on a 32 qubit neutral atom device for toxicity screening and, per the review, achieved results comparable to the best classical algorithms.
quotes: A 2022 paper by Boris Albrect and others
describes a quantum kernel running on a 32 qubit neutral atom quantum device
They achieved results comparable to the best classical algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result from other work, reported second-hand.
